title: Huntington Bank to Add Signage, Expand Presence at Regional Headquarters in Charlotte
summary: Latest investment reflects Huntington's commitment to the Carolinas CHARLOTTE, N.C., Sept. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/…...
body_markdown:
*Latest investment reflects Huntington's commitment to the Carolinas*


CHARLOTTE, N.C.


, Sept. 28, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- The Huntington National Bank (Huntington) today announced plans to add Huntington signage and expand its presence at its regional headquarters in Charlotte, underscoring the bank's long-term commitment to the Carolinas as it continues to grow across the region.


The signage will be installed at the top of the One South office tower, located at 101 S. Tryon St. in uptown Charlotte. Huntington opened its regional headquarters at One South in 2023, and today colleagues spanning its business segments, as well as a wide range of operational and support functions, are based in the building and help advance priorities across the enterprise.


Through its expansion at its regional headquarters, Huntington will occupy all of the 39th and 40th floors of One South, bringing its total space in the 40-story building to four full floors. The expansion will support Huntington's ongoing growth in North Carolina and South Carolina, adding to the several hundred colleagues already located at One South and other locations across the greater Charlotte area.


"The addition of Huntington signage and our planned expansion at our regional headquarters in Charlotte are powerful reflections of our commitment to the Carolinas and the importance of this region to our long-term strategy," said Huntington President Brant Standridge. "We are proud to mark this milestone as we continue our momentum in the Carolinas, serving individuals, businesses and communities through local relationships built on Huntington's people-first, customer-centered approach."


**Elevated Visibility in the Heart of Charlotte's Financial District**


One South, owned by Monarch Alternative Capital and Tourmaline Capital Partners and leased and managed by Trinity Partners, is a Class A building at the intersection of Trade and Tryon streets, in the heart of Charlotte's financial district. Huntington's signage will face South Tryon Street, giving the bank's name a prominent position on the city's skyline. Installation of the signage is expected in the coming weeks.


"We applaud Huntington's continued growth and investment in uptown Charlotte," said Michael J. Smith, CEO of Charlotte Center City Partners. "Their decision to double their presence at One South, a premier workspace at Trade and Tryon, further elevates uptown as a financial hub and a magnet for talent."


The signage will be fabricated and installed by SouthWood Corporation, a veteran-owned company headquartered in Rock Hill, South Carolina. Designed with programmable lighting, the signage will feature the bank's signature green and have the ability to change colors, enabling Huntington to join other buildings across uptown in recognizing community moments and other shared observances.


**Deepening Roots Across Charlotte and the Carolinas**


Huntington's planned addition of signage and expansion at its regional headquarters in Charlotte build on the significant investments it has made in the Carolinas.


Huntington has steadily grown its presence in the Carolinas over the past several years, extending its expertise and capabilities to more customers and communities throughout both states. That growth includes the bank's 2023 Commercial Banking expansion into the Carolinas; the expansion of its capital markets presence in Charlotte, a regional hub for that activity; and its 2024 announcement of plans to open approximately 55 branches across the region. As part of those plans, Huntington has opened 14 full-service branches serving 10 markets in the Carolinas, with more locations expected to come online as the branch buildout in the region continues.


Guided by its purpose of making people's lives better, helping businesses thrive and strengthening the communities it serves, Huntington has also supported organizations, initiatives and programs focused on areas important to the long-term success of the Carolinas, including affordable housing, education, financial literacy and small business formation and growth.


"We are excited to add Huntington's name to our regional headquarters in Charlotte and grow our footprint there, further demonstrating the commitment we have made to the Carolinas," said Trent Holland, regional president for North Carolina and South Carolina. "I am proud of the roots we continue to deepen in both states as we broaden the ways we are serving and supporting our customers and communities across the region."

A top 10 U.S. commercial bank, The Huntington National Bank and its affiliates provide consumers, small and middle-market businesses, corporations, municipalities, and other organizations with a comprehensive suite of banking, payments, wealth management, and risk management products and services. Founded in 1866, Huntington operates over 1,400 branches in 21 states, with certain businesses operating nationally. Visit Huntington.com for more information.
